\begin{bankq}[id=SA02-P2-PHY-S1-Q08, source={Score Advanced - Test 02 (13 May 2021)}, paper=2, qno=8, type=multi, subtopic={Properties}, answer={A,B}, answer_src=solved, working={The mirror recoils, so it oscillates and the reflected light is Doppler shifted to longer wavelengths}, difficulty=7, diff_parts={K2 S2 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: light reflected from a hanging mirror, properties | steps: momentum transfer; recoil Doppler shift; dependence of the angle}]
A mirror is hanging by a light string of length $\ell$ from ceiling. A light pulse of monochromatic light rays is incident normally on the mirror and gets reflected. Which of the following statements is/are correct ?
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Mirror will start to oscillate.}
\opt{B}{Wavelength of reflected rays will be greater than that of the incident rays.}
\opt{C}{Wavelength of reflected rays may be less than that of incident rays.}
\opt{D}{Assuming the intensity of incident light to be constant, the maximum angle to which the mirror deflects depends on the wavelength of the light pulse.}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SA04-P2-PHY-S1-Q02, source={Score Advanced - Test 04 (04 Jul 2021)}, paper=2, qno=2, type=single, subtopic={Properties}, answer={B}, answer_src=solved, working={The radio horizon is sqrt(2Rh), not sqrt(Rh)}, difficulty=3, diff_parts={K1 S1 I1 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: radio wave propagation facts | steps: radio horizon of an antenna of height h}]
Which one of the following statements is wrong?
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Radio waves in the frequency range 10MHz to 20 MHz are called sky waves}
\opt{B}{Radio horizon of the transmitting antenna for space wave is d$_\text{T}$ = $\sqrt{(\text{Rh}_\text{T})}$ (R = radius of earth, h$_\text{T}$ = height of transmitting antenna)}
\opt{C}{Fiber optical communication is almost free from electrical disturbances}
\opt{D}{The principle of fibre optical communication is total internal reflection}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SA05-P1-PHY-S1-Q03, source={Score Advanced - Test 05 (15 Jul 2021)}, paper=1, qno=3, type=single, subtopic={Properties}, answer={C}, answer_src=key, difficulty=3, diff_parts={K1 S1 I1 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: energy and intensity of an electromagnetic wave | steps: intensity I=(1/2)e0E0\^{}2 c}]

\begin{qoptions}

\end{qoptions}

\begin{bankq}[id=SA13-P1-PHY-S2-Q03, source={Score Advanced - Test 13 (13 May 2023)}, paper=1, qno=3, type=numerical, subtopic={Properties}, answer={3}, answer_src=key, difficulty=8, diff_parts={K3 S1 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: radiation pressure measured with a torsion balance, properties, force from the intensity on a vane | steps: force from the intensity on a vane; torque against the fibre}]

The angle between the equilibrium positions of the horizontal bar when the beam is switched from ``off'' to ``on'' is $\alpha$ $\times$ 10$^{-2}$ degree. The value of $\alpha$ is :-\par
\bfig{131.3}{SA13_p1_phy_s2_q03_1.png}
\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=SA17-P2-PHY-S1-Q03, source={Score Advanced - Test 17 (25 May 2023)}, paper=2, qno=3, type=single, subtopic={Properties}, answer={D}, answer_src=key, difficulty=4, diff_parts={K2 S1 I1 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: incorrect statements on a plane electromagnetic wave, properties | steps: E B and k are mutually perpendicular}, also_in={Score Advanced - Test 35 (15 May 2024) P2 Q3}]
An electromagnetic wave travelling along $z$-axis is given as: $\vec E=\vec E_0\cos(kz-\omega t)$. Choose the \textbf{INCORRECT} options from the following;
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{The associated magnetic field is given as $\vec B=\frac1c\hat k\times\vec E=\frac1\omega\left(\hat k\times\vec E\right)$}
\opt{B}{The electromagnetic field can be written in terms of the associated magnetic field as $\vec E=c\left(\vec B\times\hat k\right)$}
\opt{C}{$\hat k\cdot\vec E=0,\ \hat k\cdot\vec B=0$}
\opt{D}{$\hat k\times\vec E=0,\ \hat k\times\vec B=0$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SA18-P1-PHY-S3-Q05, source={Score Advanced - Test 18 (27 May 2023)}, paper=1, qno=5, type=numerical, subtopic={Displacement current}, answer={1.85}, answer_src=key, difficulty=8, diff_parts={K3 S1 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: magnetic field outside a region of changing electric field, displacement current, Maxwell Ampere law with the displacement current | steps: Maxwell Ampere law with the displacement current}]
An electric field of 300 V/m is confined to a circular area 10 cm in diameter. If the field is increasing at the rate of 20 V/m-s and if the magnitude of magnetic field at a point 15 cm from the centre of the circle is $B\times10^{-18}$ T, find value of $B$.
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SA23-P1-PHY-S1-Q04, source={Score Advanced - Test 23 (14 Apr 2024)}, paper=1, qno=4, type=single, subtopic={Properties}, answer={B}, answer_src=key, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K3 S1 I2 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: reflected energy fraction at normal incidence, properties, R=((n-1)/(n+1))\^{}2 | steps: R=((n-1)/(n+1))\^{}2}]
At normal incidence, a beam of light propagating in vacuum reflects off an interface with a medium of refractive index n = 2.0. The fraction of energy reflected R is given by $R=\left(\dfrac{n-1}{n+1}\right)^2$. If the percentage error in the value of n is 1\%, the percentage error in the estimation of R is :-
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{6\%}
\opt{B}{$\dfrac{16}{3}$ \%}
\opt{C}{4\%}
\opt{D}{$\dfrac83$\%}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SA23-P2-PHY-S1-Q06, source={Score Advanced - Test 23 (14 Apr 2024)}, paper=2, qno=6, type=multi, subtopic={Displacement current}, answer={A,B,C}, answer_src=key, difficulty=8, diff_parts={K3 S1 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: capacitor in an RC circuit and magnetic field between the plates, displacement current, displacement current equals conduction current | steps: displacement current equals conduction current; Ampere law}]
A circuit consists of two resistors $R_1$, $R_2$ and capacitor C as shown in figure. The capacitor consists of two circular plates with a radius b and separation d (b $\gg$ d). The key K is kept closed for a very long time. At t = 0, the key K is opened :- ($C=\dfrac{\epsilon_0\pi b^2}{d}$)\par
\bfig{108.3}{SA23_p2_phy_s1_q06_1.png}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{The magnitude of displacement current just after the key is opened is $\dfrac{V_0}{R_1+R_2}$.}
\opt{B}{The magnitude of magnetic field for r $<$ b is $B=\dfrac{\mu_0r}{2\pi b^2}\cdot\dfrac{V_0}{R_1+R_2}e^{-\frac{1}{R_1C}t}$.}
\opt{C}{The magnitude of Poynting vector for r $<$ b is $S=\dfrac{R_1V_0^2r}{2\pi db^2(R_1+R_2)^2}e^{-\frac2{R_1C}t}$.}
\opt{D}{The magnitude of Poynting vector for r $<$ b is $S=\dfrac{R_2V_0^2r}{2\pi db^2(R_1+R_2)}e^{-\frac2{R_1C}t}$.}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SA25-P2-PHY-S1-Q03, source={Score Advanced - Test 25 (21 Apr 2024)}, paper=2, qno=3, type=single, subtopic={Properties}, answer={B}, answer_src=key, difficulty=7, diff_parts={K3 S1 I2 C2 F0}, diff_note={concepts: power of scattered light measured under clouds, properties, intensity transmitted and scattered | steps: intensity transmitted and scattered}, also_in={Score Advanced - Test 26 (21 Apr 2024) P2 Q3}]
In cloudy weather, measurements are taken with a light meter pointed towards the sky. We find that, due to the scattering of light by the clouds, the incident power per unit area is approximately $I_0$, regardless of the orientation of the light meter. On top of an opaque thin walled spherical shell of radius R, there is a small hole of radius r (much larger than the wavelength of visible light). The inner side of the wall of the spherical shell is coated with soot. The intensity of illumination on the inner surface of the shell, when it is placed in the open air is :-
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$I_0\dfrac{r^2}{R^2}$}
\opt{B}{$I_0\dfrac{r^2}{4R^2}$}
\opt{C}{$I_0\dfrac{r^2}{R^2-r^2}$}
\opt{D}{$I_0\dfrac{r^2}{R^2+r^2}$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankpassage}[id=SA30-P2-PHY-S2-G8-9, source={Score Advanced - Test 30 (04 May 2024)}, questions={8-9}]
A large, flat sheet carries a uniformly distributed electric current with current per unit width J. This current creates a magnetic field on both sides of the sheet, parallel to the sheet and perpendicular to the current, with magnitude B = $\dfrac12\mu_0\mathrm J_\mathrm s$. If the current is in the y direction and oscillates in time according to J$_{\max}$ (cos $\omega$t)$\hat{\mathrm j}$, the sheet radiates an electromagnetic wave. Figure shows such a wave emitted from one point on the sheet chosen to be the origin. Such electromagnetic waves are emitted from all points on the sheet. The magnetic field of the wave to the right of the sheet is described by the wave function\par
$\vec{\mathrm B}$ = $\dfrac12\mu_0\mathrm J_{\max}$ [cos(kx $-$ $\omega$t)]$\hat{\mathrm k}$\par
\bfig{119.3}{SA30_p2_phy_s2_para8_9_1.png}
\end{bankpassage}
